energy.title: Power and energy
energy.src_auto_info: Motors are sized from the robot's weight: each axis at 2x its own gravity load, assumed servo.
energy.src_total_info: The robot's rated power from its label or datasheet, split across the axes by load (servo). Torque limits follow from it.
energy.src_labels_info: Each axis's motor label. A stepper driver draws constant current regardless of load (the W on the label); torque limit = holding torque x gear ratio.

    Z raised to the safe height of {min} cm.

>> AUTONOMOUS AVOIDANCE: obstacle detected.
>> U-turn route planned at {z} cm height.
ik.no_route: >> [!] Obstacle detected; no collision-free route found.

>> Step 1: target position vector (P_target)
   P = [ {x} cm, {y} cm, {z} cm ]^T
ik.step2: >> Step 2: inverse Jacobian & joint limits (constrained IK)
ik.step3: >> Step 3: DYNAMIC TRAJECTORY, MOTOR LOAD AND ELECTRICITY COST
ik.payload_none: - Payload           : 0.0 kg (unloaded / nominal motor speed and torque)

ik.energy_model: - Energy: joint torques from inverse dynamics (gravity + acceleration), mechanical power/efficiency + copper loss + standby

ik.energy: • Estimated energy : {wh} Wh | peak power: {peak} W
ik.saving_eco: >> SAVINGS : the economic route uses {pct}% less electricity.
ik.saving_fast: >> SAVINGS : the fast route is {pct}% cheaper (less standby and holding loss in the shorter time).

ik.torque_fast: [!] J{j}: not enough torque on the fast route ({need} > {limit} {unit}); Eco is fine
